FF7_SpellExt_Game.ini.title: Game settings
FF7_SpellExt_Game.ini.reread: Read again by "Re-init .ini files"; the keys marked start-up keep the value the game started with (the log says so).
FF7_SpellExt_Game.ini.help: The game file is flat: a line starting with [ is skipped, every key stands alone and is read by its name (case does not matter). An unknown key is logged and the rest of the file is read. A repeated key: the later line is used.

keys.name: enemy_damage_limit
keys.help: The most HP damage (or healing) one hit can do to an enemy. The game's own limit is 9999. Up to 9999999. These apply to hits ON ENEMIES, whoever makes them. Hits on party members keep the game's limits.
messages: a limit must be a number from 1 to %d
%lu is above the most allowed; using %lu

keys.name: enemy_mp_damage_limit
keys.help: The same for MP damage. The game's own limit is 999. Up to 65532. (A wrong value is logged with the HP key's range, 1 to 9999999: the DLL's wording.)
messages: a limit must be a number from 1 to %d
%lu is above the most allowed; using %lu

keys.name: atb_follows_dexterity
keys.help: yes or no (default no, the game's behaviour). yes: when a battle script changes a party member's dexterity (AI variable 40a0, e.g. a pre_action script), the DLL has the game work that member's time-gauge speed out again at once with its own routine; the gauge's fill is kept. Party slots only, not enemies. Works only when the character file defines at least one new character (the battle-start step is then in); otherwise the log says "NOT at work: it needs the battle-start hook" once. Read again with the rest of the game file (FF7_SpellExt_Characters_README.txt).
messages: atb_follows_dexterity must be yes or no

keys.name: debug
keys.help: true or false. true adds a SpellExt entry to the main menu, under Quit: a screen of debug functions (read the .ini files again, list the external spells, materia, equipment, items and characters). false, or no debug line, leaves the menu as the game's.
messages: debug must be true or false

keys.name: seats
keys.help: 2 or 4: how many new characters the game can know at once (character IDs 12-13, or 12-15). The character file may define up to 32; they take turns in the seats. 4 moves one small table of the game out of the way; use 2 if that ever gives trouble. Read when the game starts.
messages: seats must be 2 or 4

keys.name: field_entities
keys.help: Whether the new characters walk in the fields as entities of their own: off (the game's own), party (the party's new members), seats (every seated new character). See FF7_SpellExt_Field_README.txt.
messages: field_entities must be off, party or seats

keys.name: field_model_check
keys.help: yes or no: whether a character's field_model skeleton file is looked for before it is used (no: taken on trust). See FF7_SpellExt_Field_README.txt.
messages: field_model_check must be yes or no

keys.name: achievement_materia_view
keys.help: yes or no (default yes): FFNx's achievements see the new materia as the game's own (FF7_SpellExt_Materia_README.txt). With no, do not MASTER a materia of ID 91-254 and do not keep a mastered one in a save. If the game crashes while a battle is loading, do not continue from crash.ff7: new materia equipped on the original nine may show as mastered in it.
messages: achievement_materia_view must be yes or no

keys.name: wide_items
keys.help: off | shadow | on (default: off): the wide item list (FF7_SpellExt_WideItems_README.txt). Read ONCE, when the game starts. A change needs a restart of the game; "Re-init .ini files" does not change it (the log says "... STAYS ..." if the file now says something else).
messages: wide_items must be off, shadow or on

keys.name: wide_rows
keys.help: 320: the item list has the game's 320 rows. 510 (the default when the line is absent): the item list has 510 rows: the Item menu, Arrange, Customize, the shop's sell list, the Equip menu's source and the battle's Item / W-Item / Throw list. An EVEN number from 512 to 3350 (stage 4; 3350 from stage 4b, 2040 in stage 4a): the item list has that many rows (the battle list's length is moved to the DLL's own; a refusal there gives 510 rows; Arrange sorts only the rows in use); 321-509 and odd numbers are refused (510 is used). Needs wide_items = on. Read at start-up only. A save whose list uses rows past 509 is not for a build from before stage 4, and one with more than 2040 rows in use is not for the stage-4a build (FF7_SpellExt_WideItems_README.txt).
messages: wide_rows must be 320 or an even number from 510 to %d: 510 is used

keys.name: box
keys.help: off, on or auto (default auto): the box (FF7_SpellExt_Box_README.txt). auto: the box on demand, when the item list is full. Read at start-up only.
messages: box must be off, on or auto

keys.name: box_access
keys.help: save or always: where the box can be opened (FF7_SpellExt_Box_README.txt). Read at start-up only.
messages: box_access must be save or always

keys.name: box_backup
keys.help: One number, 0 to 50 (default 20): the replaced companions with a box kept per save slot; 0: deleted as before. Read at start-up only.
messages: box_backup takes one number, 0 to 50 (the replaced companions with a box kept per save slot; 0: deleted as before)

keys.name: box_throwables
keys.help: list or box: where throwable weapons go when the box takes gear (FF7_SpellExt_Box_README.txt). Read at start-up only.
messages: box_throwables must be list or box

keys.name: box_selftest
keys.help: off or on: the box's self-test at start-up (FF7_SpellExt_Box_README.txt). Read at start-up only.
messages: box_selftest must be off or on

keys.name: breaking_limits
keys.help: on or off (default off): Breaking Limits, the engine limits of FF7_SpellExt_BreakingLimits_README.txt. Read at start-up only.
messages: breaking_limits must be on or off: off is used

keys.name: wide_skeletons
keys.help: on | off | all: battle models above 48 bones (up to 127) are drawn with the DLL's bone tables (needs breaking_limits = on). all = TESTING AID, every model through the new code. Read at start-up only.
messages: wide_skeletons must be on, off or all (all: a testing aid, every battle model through the wide path): off is used

keys.name: fields_file
keys.help: The name of the field registry file in the SpellExtConfig folder (like FF7_SpellExt_Fields.ini; no drive, no .., at most 64 characters), or none: the feature stays off. See FF7_SpellExt_Fields_README.txt. Read at start-up only.
messages: fields_file takes the name of a file in the SpellExtConfig folder (like FF7_SpellExt_Fields.ini; no drive, no .., at most 64 characters), or none: the feature stays off

keys.name: fields_table_size
keys.help: auto (the highest registered field id + 1, at least 1200), or a number of field ids from 1200 to 32767. Read at start-up only.
messages: fields_table_size takes auto, or a number of field ids from 1200 to 32767: auto is used

keys.name: field_buffer_bytes
keys.help: The file buffer of a registered field, in bytes, from 4000000 to 67108864 (it can only raise the size). Read at start-up only.
messages: field_buffer_bytes takes a number of bytes from 4000000 to 67108864 (it can only raise the size): 4000000 is used

keys.name: fields_fallback
keys.help: none, or five numbers: a field of the game's own (an id from 65 to 786), x, y (-32768 to 32767), a walkmesh triangle (0 to 65535) and a direction (0 to 255), as 576, -57, -132, 31, 124: a save in a registered field holds this place. Read at start-up only.
messages: fields_fallback takes none, or five numbers: a field of the game's own (an id from 65 to 786), x, y (-32768 to 32767), a walkmesh triangle (0 to 65535) and a direction (0 to 255), as 576, -57, -132, 31, 124: none is used (a save in a registered field is saved as it is, and a field id the game cannot read is not sent anywhere)

keys.name: items_on_load
keys.help: TESTING AID: at every load the stock holds at least this many of each item: ID:count, up to 16 entries (item ID 0 to 319, or a wide item's number 1024 to 9999; count 1 to 99). 71-76 are the Power, Guard, Magic, Mind, Speed and Luck Sources. Remove the line when done.
messages: items_on_load takes up to 16 entries like 71:50 (item ID 0 to 319, or a wide item's number 1024 to 9999; count 1 to 99)

keys.name: test_drop
keys.help: TESTING AID: added to the spoils of the next battle won: up to 4 entries like 448 or 448:2 (an item ID 0 to 511, a wide item's number 1024 to 9999 or wide gear's 10000 to 27999, count 1 to 99). A line with a mistake gives nothing. Remove the line when done.
messages: test_drop takes up to 4 entries like 448 or 448:2 (an item ID 0 to 511, a wide item's number 1024 to 9999 or wide gear's 10000 to 27999, count 1 to 99): the line gives nothing

keys.name: test_steal
keys.help: TESTING AID: each ID replaces the next item gained in a battle: up to 8 item IDs like 320 448 (item ID 0 to 511, a wide item's number 1024 to 9999 or wide gear's 10000 to 27999). Remove the line when done.
messages: test_steal takes up to 8 item IDs like 320 448 (item ID 0 to 511, a wide item's number 1024 to 9999 or wide gear's 10000 to 27999): the line gives nothing

keys.name: test_stitm
keys.help: TESTING AID: each entry replaces what the next STITM of a field script gives (a chest, a thing on the ground, an event's gift): up to 8 entries like 10000 or 1024:3; count 1 to 99, else the script's own. It acts only while wide_items = on. Remove the line when done.
messages: test_stitm takes up to 8 entries like 10000 or 1024:3 (an item ID 0 to 511, a wide item's number 1024 to 9999 or wide gear's 10000 to 27999; count 1 to 99, else the script's own): the line gives nothing

keys.name: test_fill_rows
keys.help: TESTING AID: one number, 1 to 3350: the rows of the item list to fill at every load (FF7_SpellExt_WideItems_README.txt); at most the rows the list has in the run. Remove the line when done.
messages: test_fill_rows takes one number, 1 to %d (a testing aid: the rows of the item list to fill at every load)

keys.help: TESTING AID: every battle the game starts becomes this one, until the line is removed: a battle number 1 to 1023 (like 16), or scene:formation (like 4:0; scene 0 to 255, formation 0 to 3), or off. The music and the field's battle flags stay those of the battle the game chose. A line with a mistake gives nothing.

FF7_SpellExt_SpellNames.ini.title: Spell names
FF7_SpellExt_SpellNames.ini.line_format: ID  current name = new name   (like 0x1C  Fire2 = Fira)
FF7_SpellExt_SpellNames.ini.reread: Read again by "Re-init .ini files" and at every kernel load.
FF7_SpellExt_SpellNames.ini.help: One line per spell: `0x1C  Fire2 = Fira ; comment`. The ID (0 to 0xff) decides which spell is renamed. The name on the left is the game's own: leave it, it is used to find the places where other text quotes the name. The name on the right is shown: up to 24 characters (the menus were laid out for about 9). A line whose two names are the same changes nothing. Lines in [brackets] are headings. Delete the file to go back to the game's names. (FF7_SpellExt_SpellNames_README.txt)

spell names file line %d: a name must be 1 to 24 characters

FF7_SpellExt_Effects.ini.reread: Read again by "Re-init .ini files", with every effects\*.txt script; a NEW file in a mod folder is only seen after the game is restarted.
FF7_SpellExt_Effects.ini.help: [effect 0x100] to [effect 0xffff]: an effect copy (copy = and file = lines: one of the game's magic effects with some of its files replaced) or a native effect (play = and base =: a script the DLL plays). A spell names the number as its animation. [sound N], N 53848 to 58089: a sound handle, the file <game>\sfx\N.ogg played by FFNx (use_external_sfx = true). A number used twice: neither section is used. A copy with any problem is not used (all or nothing).

FF7_SpellExt_Spells.ini.title: Spells
FF7_SpellExt_Spells.ini.reread: Read again by "Re-init .ini files" (and at every kernel load). FF7_SpellExt_Spells_Test.ini, when present, is read after it as one text: IDs must not repeat between the two.
FF7_SpellExt_Spells.ini.help: Sections [3000] to [65534], one per spell, unique (a repeat is refused; the first is kept). A line in a refused section is passed over. A spell needs base, or a bytes line (or every byte set): else it is skipped. A bad line is logged and the rest of the section still loads. A comment starts with ; or # at the start of a line or after a space, so do not put " ;" or " #" inside a name or description.

keys.name: name
keys.help: Shown in menus and the cast banner, up to 31 characters (about 12 fit a column of the Magic list). Characters outside 0x20-0x7e become ?; a " becomes the game's quotation marks. (FF7_SpellExt_Spells_README.txt)

keys.help: Help line, up to 95 characters. (FF7_SpellExt_Spells_README.txt)

FF7_SpellExt_Characters.ini.help: Each new character is a section named by an ID of its own, [12] to [43]: up to 32 characters, the roster. keys.name: portrait

For more accessories, number them from 22000: WIDE ACCESSORIES, [22000] to [27999] (box = on or auto and wide_items = on in the game file). Do NOT add 10000 to an accessory number: 10000-15999 are weapons. A section numbered for another kind is NOT read, and the log says whose number it is. A section numbered for one of the game's own accessories, [288] to [319] (its item ID), changes THAT accessory of the kernel the game loaded: every key it gives replaces that field, every key it does not give keeps the kernel's value (base and give_on_load are not used there).

keys.name: base
keys.help: Required. The game's accessory to copy everything from: its number (0-31) or its item ID (288-319). 0 is the Power Wrist. Every key below overrides one thing from that copy.
messages: base must be a number
base must be one of the game's accessories: 0 to 31, or its item ID 288 to 319

keys.name: name
keys.help: Up to 31 characters.
messages: a name has at most 31 characters

keys.name: description
keys.help: Up to 95 characters.

keys.name: bonus
keys.help: Up to two stat bonuses, e.g. bonus = strength 20, magic 20. Stats: strength vitality magic spirit dexterity luck. bonus = none removes the base's bonuses.
messages: bonus must be up to two pairs like: strength 10 magic 5
each bonus needs an amount from 0 to 255

keys.name: special
keys.help: One of the game's built-in accessory effects: haste (starts battle in Haste, Sprint Shoes), berserk (always Berserk, Fury Ring), curse (Death Sentence, as the Cursed Ring), reflect (Reflect Ring), steal (better Steal, Sneak Glove), manipulate (better Manipulate, Hypno Crown), wall (Barrier and MBarrier, Protect Ring), none. An accessory has one of these at most.
messages: special must be haste, berserk, curse, reflect, steal, manipulate, wall or none

keys.name: status_defense
keys.help: Statuses it protects against, by name, e.g. status_defense = poison sleep silence. Names as in the spell file: death sleep poison sadness fury confusion silence slow stop frog small slow_numb petrify berserk paralysis darkness death_sentence ... or none.
messages: unknown status name

keys.name: element
keys.help: Elements it acts on: fire ice lightning earth poison gravity water wind holy restorative cut hit punch shoot shout hidden.
messages: unknown element name

keys.name: element_effect
keys.help: What it does with them: absorb, nullify, halve or none. Give both keys together.
messages: element_effect must be absorb, nullify, halve or none

keys.name: equip
keys.help: Who can equip it: cloud barret tifa aeris red yuffie caitsith vincent cid youngcloud sephiroth, or everyone, or none. Default: as the base. A character can also be given by its ID number: 0 Cloud, 1 Barret, 2 Tifa, 3 Aeris, 4 Red XIII, 5 Yuffie, 6 Cait Sith, 7 Vincent, 8 Cid; and 12 to 43 for the characters of the character file, by the ID of their section. Names and IDs can be mixed: equip = vincent 12. A character of the character file is allowed wherever it is seated; one made with copy_of can equip what its original is named for. A number written as 0x.... is the raw mask instead (one bit per ID up to 15; 0x1000 is the same as 12). A new character can be given by the name its section of the character file has, too (one word; capital letters do not matter). A new character can equip whatever the character named in its `equip_like` can.
messages: equip must be a list of character names or IDs (0 to 11, and 12 to 43 for the character file's), or everyone, none, or a mask as 0x....

FF7_SpellExt_Limits.ini.title: Limits
FF7_SpellExt_Limits.ini.reread: Read at start-up after the character file, and again by "Re-init .ini files" (reload_config -> reload_characters -> load_limits); a state someone is in during a battle keeps the settings it began with until the battle ends.
FF7_SpellExt_Limits.ini.help: This file gives a NEW character (one defined in the character file) limit breaks of its own. Each limit belongs to one character. A character with any section here has ONLY the limits defined here. Sections: [12] the character's own settings; [12 1-1] one limit (level 1-4, position 1-3); [12 1-1 setname] a limit of a named set (used when the character's limit_set names it); [12 state NAME] one of the character's states (up to 4); [test] testing aids for the game's own characters. Any attack key from the spell file also works in a limit's section, with the same meaning, and overrides the base limit's value.

keys.name: gauge
messages: gauge takes four numbers from 1 to 65535, one per limit level
keys.help: Four numbers, one per limit level: how slowly the gauge fills. Higher is slower. See the table below for the nine.

keys.name: learn_all_on_load
messages: expected yes or no
keys.help: yes = TESTING AID: whenever a save is loaded, every limit the character has in this file is marked learned, level 4 included. A save made afterwards keeps them. Default: no.

keys.name: full_gauge
messages: expected yes or no
keys.help: yes = TESTING AID: the character starts every battle with a full limit gauge, and any damage taken fills it again. Default: no.

keys.name: limit_set
keys.help: Which set of limits the character uses. A limit's section may carry a set name after its position: [12 1-1 barret]. Sections without one form the default set. With `limit_set = barret` only the sections tagged barret are read for this character; with `limit_set = default` (or no line) only the untagged ones. One set at a time; change the line and restart to switch. A save keeps which POSITIONS are learned, not which limits, so switching sets keeps the same positions learned. (Read before the rest of the file, from the character's own section wherever it is; the first 15 characters count, case does not matter.)

keys.name: limit_item
messages: limit_item must be one of the kernel's unused item IDs, 105 to 127
limit_item %d is already character %d's limit item: each character needs an item ID of its own (105 to 127)

keys.name: prop_offset

messages: prop_frames is all, or first-last: the frames of the animation the prop is shown on, counted from 0 (18-96; 18- = from 18 to its end)
keys.help: FIRST-LAST. keys.help: N. keys.name: state

keys.help: NAME. keys.name: hits
messages: hits is 2, 3 or 4: how many times each turn of a listed attack hits while the state lasts (1 = no change)
keys.help: N, 2 to 4. While the state lasts, each turn of one of the `commands` below hits N times instead of once, all N at that turn's one target, one straight after the other. The number of turns is the command's own. With hits = 2: Attack   1 turn  of 2 hits = 2 2x-Cut   2 turns of 2 hits = 4 4x-Cut   4 turns of 2 hits = 8 Each hit is a whole hit of its own: its own hit or miss, critical, damage and number, and the weapon's element and added effects every time. All the hits of a turn stay on the turn's target even if one of them kills it: a hit on a target that is already dead cannot miss, does its damage to nothing, and its number is shown over the dying target with no second flinch. A new target is only ever chosen per turn (retarget, below). Counter attacks, Mime, and attacks made while Berserk or Confused are the same commands and hit N times too. Default 1: no change to the hits. A state with hits = 1 still gives the listed attacks its attack scripts and its attack_targets, attack_element and long_range (until 2026-10-22 a state with hits = 1 played the model's own attack scripts). A turn gets its N hits only when it goes at ONE ENEMY: - a command that picks one of several enemies for each attack (4x-Cut) picks one per turn, and all N hits of the turn go at that one; - a turn at several targets at once (Slash-All, Flash) and a turn aimed at the party's side are left as the game has them, one hit each. While the character is a frog nothing is changed (with `ends = ... frog` the state is over by then). (Before 2026-10-13 `hits` multiplied the TURNS: with 2, Attack was two whole attacks and 4x-Cut eight, each with the game's pause between attacks. A section written then still loads; see "A section written for the older meaning" below.)

keys.name: ends

keys.help: When the prop is NOT drawn although the state lasts: none (the default: it follows the bone through everything), or a list of dead      while the character is knocked out victory   in the victory pose escape    while running away, and once escaped limit     while an animation of a limit's own pack is shown (any limit of the character's) prop_hide = victory It is never drawn while the character is a frog, while its body is hidden (summons, some limits) or is not drawn at all, and it is drawn small with a character under Mini. The limit that begins the state may have a `prop` of its own at the same bone (the second weapon being drawn from its holster, by prop_frames). While that limit's prop is there the state's is not drawn; on the frame the limit's animation is over the state's prop takes its place: never two, and none only on the frames the limit itself shows none. With the same model and the same offset, turn and scale in both there is no jump. A limit with no prop at that bone: the state's prop is drawn from the limit's effect step (ec) on. Any later limit of the character's with a prop at that bone hides the state's the same way while its own is there. While the game is paused the prop stays where it was.

keys.name: prop_colour
messages: prop_colour is body (the default: the prop is drawn with the colour and transparency the actor's body has: poisoned, petrified, fading) or own (always its own colours)
keys.help: body or own. Default body: the prop is drawn with the colour and transparency the game gives the character's body at that moment (the pulse of Poison, Berserk, Regen, Darkness, the grey of Petrify, a fade), so that it does not stand out in its hand. own = always its own colours, exactly as a limit's prop is drawn. (body has not been seen in the game yet: if a coloured prop looks wrong, use own.)

keys.name: attack_targets
messages: attack_targets is as_chosen (the default: the targets the attack was given) or all_enemies (each turn of a listed attack goes at every living enemy, with one animation)
keys.help: as_chosen or all_enemies. Default as_chosen: the attack goes at the targets it was given. all_enemies: each turn of a listed attack goes at EVERY living enemy it can be aimed at, as one record with one animation (the game's own way for Slash-All): the one-turn script (attack_script_only, or the model's own Attack) plays once and its f7 shows every enemy's number, one frame apart. The enemies are counted again at each turn: the dead and those out of reach (below) are left out; nobody left after a first turn ends the action. It goes only with hits = 1 (with more, the line is ignored and the log says so) and only to Attack, 2x-Cut and 4x-Cut; an attack aimed at the party's side (Confusion, Manipulate) is left as the game has it. The game's rule for several targets applies: each enemy takes 2/3 of the damage one target would (FUN_005de8f4), as with Slash-All or a spell cast on all. A script with a 9e in it waits for THE target to finish, and a record at several targets has none: so an action whose script has a byte 9e anywhere (the model's own 2x-Cut and 4x-Cut scripts end in one) keeps its own targets, and the log says "every enemy NOT applied". End the state's scripts with e5 ee: attack_targets     = all_enemies attack_script_only = fc 29 2a 2a f7 04 2b e5 ee In the battle menu, the target cursor of an attack that will go at every enemy sits on EVERY enemy at once, as for Slash-All or a spell cast on all: there is no single target to choose, no switch to the party's side and no L1/R1 toggle (with Mega-All too); the confirm button issues it. It shows the enemies the attack can reach: every one that can be aimed at, or only those no other stands in front of when the attack stays short range (no long_range and a short-range weapon). With every enemy hidden the confirm button only buzzes, as for a spell on all: choose another command. An attack that keeps its own targets (a 9e, above; a command not listed; a frog) keeps the game's cursor.

keys.name: attack_element
messages: attack_element is weapon (the default: the weapon's and the Elemental materia's) or element words, as a spell's element: hidden, fire ice, none
keys.help: weapon, or element words as a spell's `element` (fire, ice, lightning, earth, poison, gravity, water, wind, holy, restorative, cut, hit, punch, shoot, shout, hidden; several together; none = no element). Default weapon: the weapon's element and the Elemental materia's, as always. Anything else REPLACES both for the listed attacks while the state lasts: attack_element = hidden An element without cut, hit and punch also frees the attack from the reach rule (enemies flying out of a short weapon's reach can be hit).

keys.name: long_range
messages: long_range is yes or no (the default): whether the listed attacks are long range (no back-row halving; enemies behind others can be aimed at)
keys.help: yes or no. Default no. yes: the listed attacks are long range: no damage halving for a back row (the attacker's or the target's), and enemies standing behind others can be aimed at (the short-range bit of the weapon's targeting is taken off). The reach rule for flying enemies is the Long Range materia's and the element's (above), not this key's.

keys.name: physical_evade
messages: physical_evade is normal (the default) or 100: every physical hit on the actor misses while the state lasts
keys.help: normal or 100. Default normal. 100: while the state lasts EVERY physical hit on the character misses: a weapon-type hit, the enemies' and a confused ally's alike, whatever the attacker's luck, the character's status or the element (the game's physical hit check is answered with its own miss for the character). Magic, and the attacks that never roll to hit (fixed-damage and "always hits" specials), hit as always. A miss plays the character's own miss reaction (its dodge, script 08). Not while the character is a frog. A party member covering the character is hit by the usual rule. physical_evade = 100

keys.name: view_raise
messages: view_raise is 0 (the default) to 6000: units the battle's home view (between turns, the command menu, choosing a target) goes up while an actor is in the state
keys.help: 0 to 6000. Default 0. While the character is in the state, the battle's RESTING view (between actions, the command menu, choosing a target: the scene's own camera, wherever the game shows it) is raised by this many units, the point it looks at with it: a body held up in the air (an idle whose animation lifts the root) stays in the picture. The cameras of actions (attacks, spells, limits, the enemies') are their own, except that their first moments carry the fading lift: the view glides from the raised one into an action's camera and back, a fifth of the way each frame (gone after about 37 frames), so nothing jumps. Several characters in such states: the largest value. The view is the game's again while the character is knocked out, a frog, in the victory or escape pose, and after the state ends (it glides back down). FFNx's analogue camera (the right stick) works as before, on top of the raised view. A battle model stands about 1,300 to 1,800 units tall; a scene's camera stands about 12,000 to 17,000 units from the point it looks at. view_raise = 800

keys.name: view_back
messages: view_back is 0 (the default) to 100: per cent the battle's home view goes back from the point it looks at while an actor is in the state
keys.help: 0 to 100 (a % may follow). Default 0. With view_raise or alone: the resting view also moves this many per cent farther back from the point it looks at, so the floor and the enemies' feet stay in the picture when it is raised. view_back = 20

keys.name: pointer_raise
messages: pointer_raise is 0 (the default) to 6000: units the yellow pointer over the party member whose command menu is open goes up while the actor is in the state
keys.help: 0 to 6000. Default 0. While the character is in the state, the yellow pyramid that turns over it when its command menu is open is this many units higher. The game puts the pyramid at a fixed height for each model (from the model's own data), not at its head, so a body held up by its animations would have it below or inside it: give the same number of units as the animations lift the body. It is at the game's height again while the character is knocked out, a frog, in the victory or escape pose, and when the state ends. The target hand (when the character is chosen as a target) and the damage numbers follow the body's bones and need nothing; the status marks over the head (sleep, silence, a countdown) are not moved. pointer_raise = 1563

keys.name: script_
messages: script_NN takes the number of the model script it replaces in two hexadecimal digits: script_05 = 22 f2 e5 ee
script_00 and script_01 are the idle and the weak idle: use idle_script and idle_weak_script
script_18 to script_1b are the slots the state's attack scripts are lent in: use attack_script_only, attack_script, _next, _next2, _last
scripts 2e-32 and 34-3b are taken from the game's exe for every model, not from the model's table: a replacement would never be played
script_NN replaces a model script from 02 to 17 or 1c to 2d (3c and above are the character's limits and transformations)
this script is an action or a reaction, which the battle waits to see finished: one that ends in fe c0 never says so and would hold the battle; end it with e5 ee (or ee)
a state may replace up to 16 model scripts (script_NN lines)
a script is a list of bytes in hexadecimal, two digits each: fc f7 00 1f 9e
a state's script_NN may be up to 32 bytes
the script is empty
keys.help: While the state lasts, the character's model script NN (two hexadecimal digits) is replaced by these bytes, as idle_script replaces script 00. A reaction is a model script: 05 hurt, 06 hurt while defending, 07 the knock-out fall, 08 the dodge, 0a the big recoil, 0b the two-part recoil; casting is a model script too: 1d Magic and W-Magic, 1e Enemy Skill, 1f Summon, 20 and 21 Item (20 at the party's side, 21 at the enemies'), 21 also Throw and Coin; 13 is the Defend pose, 03 / 04 the row change, 10 an interrupted cast (ab_tool.py dump lists the model's own). Up to 16 lines a state, up to 32 bytes each; a later line for the same NN replaces it: script_05 = 22 f2 e5 ee script_08 = 23 e5 ee script_07 = 25 f2 e5 ee script_1d = e8 fc e6 ea 29 2a 2a ec 2d 2d 2d 2d 2d e5 ee (the hurt, the dodge and the fall played from animations 0x22, 0x23, 0x25; Magic as a wind-up, a hold twice, the spell's effect step ec, then animation 0x2d five times while the spell plays.) Not taken: 00 and 01 (idle_script, idle_weak_script), 18 to 1b (the attack scripts' slots), 2e-32 and 34-3b (the game takes those from its exe for every model), 33 and 3c up (the limits and transformations). A script that the battle waits for (every one but 02, 0c, 0d, 0e and 13, the standing poses) must END: one that ends in fe c0 is refused, because it would never say it has finished and the battle would wait for ever. A long one is safe: the action is over when the effect has finished AND the character has, whichever is later. Like idle_script, a script that loops (fe c0) is started again from its first byte as its animation's number. The scripts are lent when the state begins and given back when it ends; a script the character is playing at that moment (the knock-out fall that ends the state with `ends = ko`) plays to its end first, and only then is the model's own put back. Animations 0x2c-0x33 are the loaded limit pack's: a script that names them needs that pack still loaded (a state with limit_gauge = frozen keeps it).
